runs.reason:
UKMTO-reported projectile strikes on merchant ships in the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman and Arabian Gulf have been a near-daily feature of November, not a rare shock. On incident dates from 1–22 November, verified attack warnings fall on about 15 of 22 days (roughly two-thirds), including five of the seven days from 16–22 November, with single-day gaps rather than multi-day pauses.

That rate is the right anchor for 26 November. It is not higher only because the official threat label is severe: JMIC has kept the strait at SEVERE (“deliberate hostile action highly likely”) while quiet days have still occurred.

What moves this day up from a flat two-thirds is that the campaign is still live and the target set has not disappeared. On 22 November UKMTO logged multiple eastbound projectile strikes in the strait (warnings 219-26, 220-26 and 221-26) plus a bulk carrier hit at Dibba anchorage (218-26). JMIC’s 22 November outlook said further attacks on tankers on the Omani side were highly likely, and gCaptain counted about ten tanker strikes in a week. US-facilitated transits were still about 38 a day on 19–21 November. As of 24 November, US–Iran talks were still stalled and Iran was still claiming strikes. Time-late reporting is normal, so a 26 November hit would still count if UKMTO or JMIC issued the warning afterward.
